questions.answer: Lots of different sports club along with even more societies which hosted plenty of social events - great information about this at the intro day

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: I liked the scribble society and the hiking club. Was fun even if you didnt know a ton of other people.

questions.answer: Definetly go on one of the trips around the country arranged by the international students society.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Quite easy - nothing to different

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Just be friendly - everyone else is

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: Nothing really

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: General friendly attitude - easy to strike up a conversation

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer:
Most important would be to start the search for an accomadation quite early. The housing market in Ireland is in a really dire state so the earlier the better really. Even if some of the private student accomadation rooms seems very expensive, book it anyways - most accomadation cost around 10.000kr a month, and its better to just have somewhere to live. 
Second - take advantage of student clubs and societies!
Third - dont be paranoid if parts of the application process seems very late and last minute - everything lines up in the end

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: Busses in Cork are quite cheap, but not very punctual, so if you can try and live close by campus

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: Learning to be extremly independent

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Have to take on almost everything by myself - you cant rely as much on friends and family as usual

questions.question: Any other comments?
Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
